pages.title: The Black Hole Era
pages.text: $(thing)The Black Hole Era$()$(br2)After the protons, only black holes are left, slowly radiating. A black hole of a solar mass needs 10^67 years to evaporate, a supermassive one 10^100 - and then it ends in a flash. Unlocks the Last Flash of a Black Hole.

$(thing)Insight$(): 190$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Eschatology, Singularity Physics, The Holographic Principle.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Hawking Emitter.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A black hole radiates as a black body at a temperature inversely proportional to its mass, so it loses mass at a rate dM/dt = −ħc⁴/(15360πG²M²) and gets brighter as it shrinks. Separate the variables and write the total time it needs to radiate away a mass M completely.
